etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French cavalerie, in turn from Italian cavalleria. Recorded in English from the 1540s. Doublet of chivalry.

definitions.definition: (military, usually historical, uncountable) The military arm of service that fights while riding horses.

quote.citation: 1891, A[rthur] Conan Doyle, chapter XXXIII, in The White Company, New York, N.Y., Boston, Mass.: Thomas Y[oung] Crowell & Company […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Two hundred heavily-armed cavalry rode behind the Audley standard, while close at their heels came the Duke of Lancaster with a glittering train, heralds tabarded with the royal arms riding three deep upon cream-colored chargers in front of him.

definitions.definition: (military, countable) An individual unit of this arm of service.
(military, countable) The branch of the military transported by fast light vehicles, also known as mechanized cavalry.
(figurative) A source of rescue, especially in an emergency.

quote.citation: 2015 February 1, Howard Tayler, Schlock Mercenary‎[1], archived from the original on 14 May 2024:
quote.text: "We landed in their killbox?"  "We did.  I am sor...  No, belay that.  Heads down!  Cavalry incoming!"
